GuideHeading: How to connect Coolify Deploy Manager
Guide1Body: In Coolify, enable API access under Settings → Access and API. Allowed IPs may limit clients; access via managed SSH tunnel is forwarded through your VPS.
Guide2Body: In Keys & Tokens → API Tokens, create ONE token with READ and DEPLOY only. Do not enable Root, Write or Read Sensitive Data.
Guide3Body: Direct connection: trusted HTTPS, or private LAN/VPN HTTP without a domain. Public-IP HTTP: select the automatic SSH tunnel. A dedicated SSH key can be installed with the copyable VPS command.
Guide4Body: Click Refresh. CDM checks /api/health and reads the inventory. A read-only test does not verify deploy permissions; these are checked when submitting a deployment.
Guide5Body: CDM identifies staging, production and release from names, branches and environments. Conflicting signals remain unclassified. Verify targets before deploying.

Guide6Body:
A personalized CDM clone (.exe), .pending file or .bak backup contains API tokens and, if configured, a private SSH key.
1. Sign in to Coolify in your browser: Keys & Tokens → API Tokens → Revoke token. Revoke every token used by the lost clone.
2. If SSH tunneling was enabled, use your VPS provider's console or a separate working SSH key. Sign in as the SAME SSH user configured in CDM and open: nano ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. Identify CDM's public-key line by comparing it with the saved public key or its fingerprint; delete ONLY that line and save. Do not remove other keys. If unsure which line is CDM's, do not delete one at random.
3. Generate a new Coolify API token and a new dedicated SSH key using the generic CDM executable.
IMPORTANT: Revoking an API token does not revoke SSH access; both credentials must be invalidated separately.
